title: OA Capstone — Wrapped & Company-Specific Questions
relevance: Online assessments and interviews stress disguised aptitude patterns—binary bit tricks, work/speed rates, path counting, and expected-value probability—under speed and accuracy pressure.
company_notes: Cisco OA; Product-SDE OAs tagged Amazon/Microsoft/Uber; Quant/trading styles associated with Optiver, SIG, Jane Street, and D.E. Shaw.

phases.goal: Establish the core OA pattern families: nibble/popcount reading, functional/set identities, rates and means, grid paths, and basic probability/EV setups.

must_hit.point: A value written as coefficients times 4096, 256, 16, and 1 can be read as separate 4-bit nibbles when each coefficient is strictly less than 16, so set bits are counted per nibble without forming the base-10 sum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate maps powers to 2^12, 2^8, 2^4, 2^0 and popcounts the nibbles (e.g. 0011 1111 0101 0011 → 10).

must_hit.point: Equal-distance round-trip average speed is the harmonic mean 2xy/(x+y), not the arithmetic mean of the two speeds.
must_hit.evidence_hint: For 60 km/h out and 40 km/h back they give 4800/100 = 48 km/h, and reject naive 50.

must_hit.point: Shortest grid paths with only North/East moves from (0,0) to (5,5) equal choosing 5 East moves among 10 total moves, and that count is 252.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States exactly 5 East + 5 North and writes the count as 252.

must_hit.point: Successive percentage changes of +a% then −a% net to a decrease of (a^2)/100 percent, not zero.
must_hit.evidence_hint: For +20% then −20% they conclude a 4% decrease via 20^2/100.

probes: Why is 45×45 − 44×46 equal to 1 without multiplying out both products?
A shuttle every 15 minutes: why is P(wait > 10 minutes) equal to 1/3?

hints.1: Look for algebraic identities or uniform waiting windows before computing.
hints.2: Difference of squares for the product; wait > 10 means arrival in the first 5 minutes of a 15-minute cycle.
hints.3: 44×46 = 45^2 − 1 so the expression is 1; probability is 5/15 = 1/3.

phases.goal: Show step-by-step solution mechanics for work-rate leftovers, complement counting, LCM alignment, painted-cube borders, and Bayes/coupon-collector setups.

must_hit.point: With A at 1/12 and B at 1/15 per minute, after 4 minutes of combined work the remaining fraction is 2/5, which B alone finishes in 6 minutes.
PINs with at least one repeated digit use complement: 10^4 total minus 10×9×8×7 no-repeat PINs equals 4960.
Two tokens with 12 and 15 states realign after a number of state-steps equal to their LCM, which is 60, so token A needs 60/12 = 5 full cycles.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names LCM 60 and divides by 12 to get 5.

must_hit.point: For a rare disease at 1% prevalence with a 99%-accurate test (1% false positive and 1% false negative), P(disease | positive) is 50% by Bayes.

probes: Walk through the painted cube: side 18 cm into 729 unit cubes; how do you get 64 with at least one red and one blue?
How do you set up expected rolls to see all six faces on a fair die?

hints.1: Separate which faces give red vs blue, or sum waiting times for each new coupon.
hints.2: Red on top/bottom; blue on sides → border rings of each 9×9 face: 81−49=32 each, total 64; coupon terms 6/(6−k).

phases.goal: Contrast product-OA speed/accuracy habits with quant-style EV reasoning and conditional profit, including keep-vs-reroll thresholds.

must_hit.point: Product OAs emphasize brute-force speed and accuracy, while quant interviews emphasize out-loud reasoning and risk management.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly contrasts those two interview styles from the intro.

must_hit.point: Optimal single-die keep-or-reroll-once keeps only faces strictly above the one-roll EV 3.5 (i.e. 4, 5, 6), yielding EV 4.25.
In the uniform-V bid problem with resale 1.5V, conditional expected profit given winning is negative for any positive bid, so the optimal bid is $0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions winner’s curse / E[profit|win]=−0.25B and chooses B=$0.

probes: When should you use harmonic mean instead of averaging two speeds?
Why is bidding halfway between $0 and $1000 not optimal in the car-value puzzle?

hints.1: Equal distances weight time differently; winning a bid is a selected sample of V.
hints.2: More time is spent at the slower speed; E[V|V≤B]=B/2 so 1.5·(B/2)−B < 0.
hints.3: Harmonic mean → 48 km/h not 50; optimal bid is $0.

phases.goal: Apply the same patterns to clock/calendar/set/boat/tank and guarantee/data-sufficiency OA staples under time pressure.

must_hit.point: Hands opposite between 4 and 5: minute hand must gain 50 minute-spaces at 55 spaces per 60 minutes, giving 54 6/11 minutes past 4.
In a class of 100 with 60 cricket, 50 football, and 20 neither, both sports equals 30 via |C∪F|=80 = 60+50−|intersection|.
With 10 black and 10 white identical socks, pigeonhole guarantee of a matching pair requires drawing 3 socks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Worst case one of each color then the third matches; answer 3 not 11.

must_hit.point: Data sufficiency can leave C undetermined even with both statements: A+B+C=60 and A−B=10 still leave 2B+C=50 with two unknowns.

probes: A dishonest dealer uses 900 g for a kg at cost price—what is the gain percent, and why divide by the false weight?
Boat: 24 km upstream in 6 h and 20 km downstream in 4 h—what is still-water speed?

hints.1: Profit is true-minus-false relative to what was actually given; still water averages up and down speeds.
hints.3: Gain is 11 1/9%; still-water speed is 4.5 km/h.

tradeoffs.topic: Product-SDE OA speed/accuracy vs quant out-loud EV reasoning
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Product OAs reward fast, exact pattern execution (rates, combinatorics, means). Quant screens reward narrating strategy, thresholds, and risk (keep-vs-reroll, conditional profit), not just the final number.

tradeoffs.topic: Arithmetic mean of speeds vs harmonic mean
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Equal-distance round trips use 2xy/(x+y). Averaging 60 and 40 to 50 is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed; the true average is 48 km/h.

tradeoffs.topic: Keep first die roll vs reroll once
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Compare the roll to the continuation value 3.5: keep 4–6, reroll 1–3. That optimal policy raises EV from 3.5 to 4.25.

tradeoffs.topic: Positive bid vs bid $0 under winner’s curse
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Winning only when V≤B makes E[V|win]=B/2; with resale 1.5V, expected profit given a win is −0.25B, so any positive bid loses in expectation and $0 is optimal.

gotchas.trap: Averaging outbound and return speeds (60 and 40) as 50 km/h.
gotchas.correction: Use the harmonic mean for equal distances: 2×60×40/(60+40)=48 km/h; more time is spent at the slower speed.

gotchas.trap: Assuming +20% then −20% returns to the original consumption.
gotchas.correction: Net change is a decrease of (20^2)/100 = 4%.

gotchas.trap: Bidding a “reasonable” positive amount for the car because resale is 1.5V.
gotchas.correction: Condition on acceptance: E[profit|win]=−0.25B < 0 for B>0, so optimal bid is $0 (winner’s curse).

gotchas.trap: Treating a 99%-accurate disease test at 1% prevalence as ~99% PPV after a positive.
gotchas.correction: Bayes gives P(D|T)=50% when false-positive mass among the healthy nearly matches true positives.

gotchas.trap: Thinking data-sufficiency statements that constrain A, B, C jointly always determine C.
gotchas.correction: A+B+C=60 and A−B=10 yield only 2B+C=50—still insufficient for a unique C.

gotchas.trap: Requiring 11 socks to guarantee a matching pair among two colors.
gotchas.correction: With two colors, three draws guarantee a pair by the pigeonhole principle.
